brand.name: CommonGlot
brand.tagline: Open language technology for every language
brand.description: CommonGlot is the open home of GlotSuite: language identification, script detection, web corpora, models and benchmarks for the world's under-served languages, plus a public directory of what technology exists for each language and script.

title: Language tech
for the
long tail.
home.lead: Most language technology serves a few dozen languages. CommonGlot builds and documents the open tools, corpora and benchmarks that reach the rest — and keeps a public record of what exists for every language and every script.

directory_teaser.title: A booklet for every language and script
directory_teaser.text: Like Glottolog or Ethnologue, but focused on technology: each language and writing system gets its own page listing where it is spoken, how it is written, how endangered it is, and which identification models, corpora, language models and OCR systems support it today.

home.projects_text: Eight open releases, one pipeline. Every model, dataset and tool is free to use.

cta.title: Is your language missing?
cta.text: Corrections, data and evaluations from language communities are the fastest way to improve coverage. Open an issue or send a pull request — every booklet links to its sources.

mission.title: Every language deserves working technology.
mission.statement: We build and maintain free, open language technology for the thousands of languages that commercial systems ignore — and we publish an honest, inspectable record of what does and doesn't exist for each of them.
paragraphs: Over 7,000 languages are spoken today, yet the web corpora, language models and OCR engines that power modern NLP cover only a small fraction of them. When a language can't be identified, it can't be collected; when it can't be collected, no model learns it; when no model learns it, its speakers are left out.

CommonGlot breaks that chain at each link. GlotLID and GlotScript identify languages and writing systems. GlotCC, GlotWeb and our smaller corpora collect text. Glot500 turns it into models. GlotOCR Bench measures how well today's systems read the world's scripts. Everything is released under open licences.
Alongside the tools, we maintain a directory that is part catalogue and part audit: one booklet per language and per script, built from public sources, showing exactly which technologies support it.

pillars.title: Identify
pillars.text: Know which language and script a text is in — the first step for any corpus.

pillars.title: Collect
pillars.text: Find and clean web text for languages that big crawls miss.

pillars.title: Model
pillars.text: Train and release multilingual models that include the long tail.

pillars.title: Evaluate
pillars.text: Benchmark systems per language and per script so gaps are visible.

pillars.title: Document
pillars.text: Keep a public directory of what technology exists for each language.

principles.title: Open by default
principles.text: Code, models and data packaging are released under permissive licences (Apache-2.0, MIT, CC0) wherever the source allows.

principles.title: Every claim has a source
principles.text: Directory entries are generated from Glottolog, GlotScript, LinguaMeta and our own releases, and link back to them.

principles.title: Coverage over headlines
principles.text: We report per-language and per-script results, not just averages that hide the long tail.

principles.title: Communities first
principles.text: Speakers know their languages best. Corrections and contributions from communities take priority.

deliverables.label: Identification
deliverables.title: Language & script identification
deliverables.text: Models and libraries that tell you what language and writing system a piece of text is in — for 2,000+ language labels and every Unicode script.

deliverables.label: Corpora
deliverables.title: Web-scale and curated corpora
deliverables.text: Clean, documented text for minority languages: a CommonCrawl corpus for 1,000+ languages, a web index for 400+, and smaller curated collections.

deliverables.label: Models
deliverables.title: Multilingual language models
deliverables.text: Pretrained encoders that extend coverage from about a hundred languages to more than five hundred.

deliverables.label: Benchmarks
deliverables.title: Benchmarks and leaderboards
deliverables.text: Evaluation that is broken down by script and language, so you can see who is served and who is not.

deliverables.label: Directory
deliverables.title: The language & script directory
deliverables.text: A booklet per language and per script, combining Glottolog metadata with GlotSuite coverage. Browse it on this site or download it as JSON.

glotsuite.title: GlotSuite
glotsuite.lead: GlotSuite is the family of research releases at the heart of CommonGlot. Each project solves one link in the chain from raw web text to working language technology, and each one feeds the next.

pipeline.label: Identify
pipeline.text: GlotLID labels the language, GlotScript the writing system.

pipeline.label: Collect
pipeline.text: GlotCC and GlotWeb gather and filter web text with those labels.

pipeline.label: Model
pipeline.text: Glot500 learns from the collected corpora.

pipeline.label: Evaluate
pipeline.text: GlotOCR Bench and per-language results show where gaps remain.

adoption.title: Corpus filtering
adoption.text: GlotLID is used as a language filter in large open multilingual web corpora, including FineWeb-2.

adoption.title: Research baselines
adoption.text: Glot500-m is a standard baseline for massively multilingual evaluation of tail languages.

adoption.title: Script-aware pipelines
adoption.text: GlotScript is installed from PyPI to detect and split scripts in multilingual preprocessing.

data_page.title: Everything on this site is a JSON file.
data_page.lead: The site is static and every page renders from the files below. Use them directly, mirror them, or rebuild them from the upstream sources with one script.

files.title: Language index
files.text: One compact row per language: ISO 639-3, name, macroarea, family, endangerment, scripts, coordinates, speakers and GlotSuite coverage flags.

files.title: Language details
files.text: Booklet data sharded by the first letter of the ISO code: endonym, countries, Glottocode, Wikidata ID, documentation level, auxiliary scripts, GlotLID per-label metrics and Glot500 labels.

files.title: Scripts
files.text: One record per ISO 15924 script: name, type, direction, Unicode ranges, specimen, languages using it, GlotLID label count and per-model OCR results.

files.title: OCR models
files.text: GlotOCR Bench summary per model: overall, high/mid/low-tier accuracy and macro CER.

files.title: Projects
files.text: GlotSuite projects with descriptions, links, usage snippets and BibTeX.

files.title: Statistics
files.text: Counts derived when the data was last built.

files.title: Site copy
files.text: All page text, navigation and team information.

files.title: Vocabularies
files.text: Labels and colours for macroareas, endangerment levels, coverage flags and script types.

data_page.rebuild_code:
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/glottolog/glottolog-cldf src/glottolog-cldf
for r in GlotScript GlotLID GlotWeb GlotOCR-bench; do
  git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/cisnlp/$r src/$r
done
pip install pycountry
python3 tools/build_data.py --sources src

sources.name: Glottolog
sources.use: Names, Glottocodes, families, macroareas, coordinates, endangerment, documentation level

sources.name: GlotScript-R
sources.use: Writing systems per language, Unicode ranges per script

sources.name: GlotLID v3
sources.use: Supported labels and per-label F1 / precision / recall

sources.name: GlotOCR Bench
sources.use: Per-script OCR accuracy and CER for 14 models

about.title: Who we are
about.lead: CommonGlot grew out of the GlotSuite research line at the Center for Information and Language Processing (CIS), LMU Munich, in collaboration with Sorbonne Université and CNRS. It brings those releases under one open roof.

team.name: Amir Hossein Kargaran
team.role: Lead of GlotLID, GlotScript, GlotCC, GlotOCR Bench

team.name: Ayyoob Imani
team.role: Lead of Glot500, co-author of GlotLID

about.team_note: Plus the many co-authors of Glot500 and the open-source contributors who report issues and send data.

contribute.title: Report an error
contribute.text: Wrong name, script or coverage flag? Open an issue on the site repository and link the booklet.

contribute.title: Share data
contribute.text: Point us to openly licensed text in your language, or to websites GlotWeb should index.

contribute.title: Evaluate
contribute.text: Test GlotLID, Glot500 or OCR models on your language and share the results.

contribute.title: Improve the site
contribute.text: Everything is static HTML + JSON. Pull requests are welcome.

faq.a: No. It is an open umbrella for research releases and community work on language technology for minority languages.

faq.q: Where does the directory data come from?
faq.a: From Glottolog, GlotScript, LinguaMeta and GlotSuite releases, combined by a public build script. See the Open data page for every source and licence.

faq.q: A language says “not covered” but I know a model exists.
faq.a: The directory currently tracks GlotSuite coverage plus OCR benchmark results. Please open an issue — adding other open technologies is on the roadmap.
Each project page has a BibTeX entry with a copy button. Please cite the specific project you use.

footer.blurb: Open tools, corpora, models and benchmarks for the world's under-served languages — and a public directory of what exists for each one.
footer.legal: Code and site content are open source. Directory data © their respective sources — see Open data.

languages_page.title: Every language, and the technology that serves it.
languages_page.lead: Search, filter and map thousands of languages. Each one opens a booklet with its location, family, writing systems, endangerment status and which GlotSuite technologies support it.
languages_page.coverage_text: Share of languages in each group that GlotLID can identify. Gaps show where identification — and therefore corpus collection — is still missing.
languages_page.families_text: The largest language families in the current selection, with how many of their languages GlotLID covers.

scripts_page.title: Every writing system in Unicode, and how well machines read it.
scripts_page.lead: Each ISO 15924 script gets a booklet: a specimen, its Unicode ranges, the languages written in it, identification support and per-model OCR accuracy from GlotOCR Bench.
scripts_page.ocr_text: Average Acc@5 per model on GlotOCR Bench (plain rendering). High = Latin; mid and low tiers cover the remaining scripts.

booklet.language_tech_text: Which open technologies support this language today. Entries come from GlotSuite releases and the GlotOCR benchmark.
booklet.not_covered: Not covered yet — help us change that.
booklet.sources_note: Booklet built from Glottolog, GlotScript, LinguaMeta and GlotSuite data. See Open data for licences.

not_found.title: This page wandered off.
not_found.text: The page you were looking for doesn't exist. Try the language or script directory instead.
